raw_response.headline_result_summary: Analyzing 13,376 Ministry of Water Resources (MWR) National Rural Drinking Water Safety Project investments across Guizhou Province (2010-2013; regression N = 61 counties out of 82 total), Pizzi (2020) finds that local officials' implementation discretion and short-term completion pressures override national pro-minority policy: counties with a higher ethnic-minority population share receive significantly less drinking water infrastructure funding and have significantly fewer project beneficiaries (Table 2 Model 1 beta = -83,928.93, p < 0.01; Full Model 2 beta = -75,817.29, p < 0.05; Multilevel Model 12 beta = -70,883.79, p < 0.05). Crucial nuance for legal/institutional coding: if the focal exposure is instead formal legal Minority Regional Autonomy (Autonomous County or Autonomous Prefecture) or Co-ethnic Leadership (Share Han Leaders), their additive main effects on project beneficiaries are statistically null once minority share and controls are included (Autonomous County beta = -41,810.91, SE = 25,959.55 in Model 2; 1,437.54, SE = 24,414.71 in Multilevel Model 12; Share Han Leaders beta = -26,776.74, SE = 31,165.39), though county autonomy significantly moderates the minority-share slope (Table 4 Model 3: Minority x Autonomous = +283,665, p < 0.05; Autonomous County = -236,074.3, p < 0.05, reversing the negative minority slope within autonomous counties and yielding a positive net autonomy effect only above ~83.2% minority share).
raw_response.specification_or_coding_pitfalls: 1. CHOICE OF FOCAL EXPOSURE (DISCRETIONARY IMPLEMENTATION / ETHNIC SHARE vs. FORMAL AUTONOMOUS LEGAL STATUS vs. LEADER ETHNICITY): The paper's headline independent variable is Percentage Minority (consistently negative and p < 0.05 across all beneficiary and funding models, demonstrating discretionary implementation disadvantage against minority areas). However, the formal legal/institutional variables tested as 'Alternative Explanations'—Autonomous County, Autonomous Prefecture, and Share Han Leaders—have statistically NULL additive main effects in controlled regressions (Table 2 Model 2; Table A5 Models 12-13), a borderline negative p < 0.10 effect of Autonomous County on funding (-2,173.5*, Table A3 Model 6), a negative significant effect of Autonomous County only when Percentage Minority is omitted (p. 624), and a MIXED/conditional interaction in Table 4 Model 3 (Autonomous County = -236,074.3**, Minority x Autonomous = +283,665**). 2. INTERACTION EXTRAPOLATION TRAP (TABLE 4 MODEL 3): Because all 11 autonomous counties are 50% to 95.7% minority (mean 74.8%), the -236,074.3** constituent coefficient on Autonomous County (at 0% minority) is out-of-sample; conversely, the positive +283,665** interaction does not mean autonomous counties get more beneficiaries across the board—the linear combination (-236,074.3 + 283,665 * Minority) is negative at the autonomous-county mean (74.8%) and only turns positive above 83.2% minority share. 3. OUTCOME IS INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECT BENEFICIARIES / FUNDING, NOT VERIFIED HOUSEHOLD TAP FUNCTIONALITY: The author explicitly notes (pp. 616, 626) that MWR records track cumulative authorized/completed project beneficiaries and funds (with approved-but-uncompleted projects coded as 0, fn. 3), without follow-up household data on whether completed facilities actually succeeded in delivering safe drinking water. 4. PUBLISHED TYPESETTING / UNIT ERRORS IN TABLES: (a) In Table 2 Model 1 (PDF p. 15), the Geographic Controls rows are shifted up by one line so Karst Landform (106,976.40**) is printed on the Total Water Points line, Slope (6,510.96) on the Karst line, and Constant (-99,780.18) duplicated on the Slope line; (b) Funding figures in Tables 1, 3, A2, A3, and A5 are in 10,000 RMB (wan yuan) units (mean 6,671.59 = RMB 66.71 million per p. 616), and text p. 622 mistakenly cites RMB 149,000 vs. 114,000 (confusing beneficiary counts with RMB); (c) multiplication signs ('x') are dropped in Table 4 and Table A4 headers/rows; (d) Table A5 Model 13 prints ** on Percentage Minority (-3,136.75, SE 1,682.30) even though z = -1.865 (p ~ 0.062). 5. LISTWISE DELETION: Descriptive Table 1 uses all N = 82 counties, whereas all regressions use N = 61 due to missing karst and village-count controls.
raw_response.study_design: Cross-sectional county-level observational study (aggregating 13,376 Ministry of Water Resources rural drinking water infrastructure projects authorized in 2010-2013 across Guizhou Province counties, analyzed with OLS regressions with robust standard errors and prefecture-nested multilevel models, supplemented by field visits to >50 villages and interviews)
raw_response.unit_and_sample_size: Counties in Guizhou Province, China: N = 82 total counties in descriptive statistics (aggregating 13,376 MWR drinking water projects from 2010-2013 and CVs of 360 county governors and CCP Party secretaries); N = 61 counties in all multivariable OLS models and N = 61 counties nested in 9 prefectures in multilevel models.
